permutationLabel: Recurrent occult/overt bleeding, aortic stenosis, aspirin
summary: 76-year-old woman with aortic stenosis, CKD and aspirin for coronary disease; recurrent iron-deficiency anaemia (Hb 8.6, ferritin 8) with intermittent dark red bleeding. Colorectal cancer must be excluded; angiodysplasia is the working diagnosis; aspirin for secondary prevention is continued.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Tiredness and intermittent dark blood in the stool
inputs.hpi: Six months of tiredness and breathlessness on exertion. Intermittent small amounts of dark red blood mixed with stool. Two blood transfusions this year for anaemia. OGD three months ago: normal. No change in bowel habit, no weight loss. Moderate aortic stenosis, ischaemic heart disease (stent 2019) on aspirin, CKD stage 3.

exam.general: Pale conjunctivae. HR 84 regular, BP 138/64. Ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids.
exam.other: PR: dark blood-streaked stool on the glove, no mass.

imaging.name: OGD (3 months ago)
imaging.result: Normal oesophagus, stomach and duodenum. Duodenal biopsies normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Iron-deficiency anaemia with intermittent lower GI bleeding — suspected colonic angiodysplasia
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Recurrent iron-deficiency anaemia with intermittent lower GI bleeding; suspected colonic angiodysplasia (aortic stenosis). Colorectal cancer to be excluded by colonoscopy.

mustNotMiss.note: Iron-deficiency anaemia at 76 with bleeding: colorectal cancer must be on the differential until colonoscopy.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Angiodysplasia is not a PANE disease; only the iOS ClinicalPathwayEngine GI-haemorrhage list names it.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No output requests ferritin/iron studies for IDA with bleeding (the plan is the ischaemic-colitis protocol).
No iron replacement anywhere in the plan (no IDA rule reads Hb/MCV/ferritin).
No endoscopic therapy (argon plasma coagulation) — there is no angiodysplasia protocol.

mustExclude.note: Therapeutic heparin in an actively bleeding patient is harmful.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: ICD K55.21 (angiodysplasia of colon with haemorrhage) matches the ischaemic_colitis protocol (prefix K55), whose medications include a therapeutic heparin infusion (for mesenteric venous thrombosis) — offered to a bleeding patient.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Exclude K55.2x (angiodysplasia) from the ischaemic_colitis protocol prefixes; add an angiodysplasia/LGIB protocol (colonoscopy + APC, iron, continue secondary-prevention aspirin).

mustExclude.note: BSG 2019: aspirin for secondary cardiovascular prevention should not be stopped routinely in LGIB (coronary stent).

mustExclude.knownGapNote: Same K55 → ischaemic_colitis routing: "broad-spectrum IV antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam)" and NBM for an outpatient with angiodysplasia.

guideline.name: BSG guideline — diagnosis and management of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Angiodysplasia: endoscopic therapy (argon plasma coagulation); antiplatelets for secondary prevention continued
guideline.citation: Oakland K, Chadwick G, East JE, et al. Diagnosis and management of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding: guidelines from the British Society of Gastroenterology. Gut. 2019;68:776–789.

guideline.name: BSG guideline — management of iron deficiency anaemia in adults
guideline.section: IDA in men and post-menopausal women: bidirectional endoscopy (colonoscopy if OGD negative); iron replacement
guideline.citation: Snook J, Bhala N, Beales ILP, et al. British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for the management of iron deficiency anaemia in adults. Gut. 2021;70:2030–2051.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — suspected cancer: recognition and referral (lower gastrointestinal tract cancers)
guideline.section: Lower GI: age ≥ 60 with iron-deficiency anaemia → suspected colorectal cancer pathway
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (NG12). First published 2015; lower GI recommendations updated 2023 to incorporate DG56.

rationale: Permutation: occult/overt recurrent bleeding with IDA, antiplatelet for a coronary stent. ICD K55.21 (angiodysplasia of colon with haemorrhage, ICD-10-CM) sits under the K55 vascular-disorders block; this checks whether angiodysplasia is routed to the ischaemic-colitis protocol (antibiotics, heparin infusion, colectomy).
